title: WIN-014: gravitational sensitivity-floor defense neutralization
defense_summary: The dome's defense is that the null result at C1-C4 does not refute WIN-014 because the gravimeters (especially the 7 LaCoste-Romberg spring instruments) may not be sensitive enough to detect the predicted κ-gravity signal. The 3-9 µGal κ prediction could fall within or below the LCR noise floor (~1-2 µGal post-fit residuals), so absence of signal is absence of detection, not absence of effect.
analyst_brief: Develop a formal defense neutralization for the sensitivity-floor argument. Key considerations: (1) the SG-053 is rated to 0.1-1 µGal precision — well below the 3-9 µGal prediction; if the dome accepts the null result from SG-053 as WIN-014's confirmation, it cannot simultaneously invoke sensitivity-floor for the same instrument; (2) the 2013 CJG abstract itself says 'the supposed gravity anomaly cannot be detected at present with actual observation conditions and instrument performance' — this is the authors' own hedged language, but the dome cites the same paper as WIN-014 confirmation; (3) the either-way dilemma already in detail_evidence (ISS-2712 patch) handles the logical structure; the EXP should add quantitative instrument-capability grounding and a formal closure on the 'maybe SG-053 is also too noisy' sub-defense. Cite SG-053 performance specs if available.
